notes: Each valid record validates against the schema and passes the semantic invariants S1-S12 listed in the schema's $comment. Each invalid case applies its JSON Patch ops (RFC 6902) to the named valid record; rejected_by says whether the schema or a named semantic invariant rejects it. An op value of the form {"$generate": {"repeat": c, "count": n}} stands for a string of n copies of c. The migration case's inputs are illustrative extracts: the v1 record validates against Plans/home_workspace_layout.schema.json, editor_groups stands for the editor's own workspace state (editor_workspace_state.v1) and terminal_sections for the terminal section, workgroup, pane and session records; expected_v2 is the record SP-330's conversion produces.

migration.name: v1_four_editor_panels_dashboard_two_terminal_sections_floating_chat
migration.description: Four v1 editor panels (two shown, one hidden with a tab, one hidden and empty), a dashboard docked left, two terminal sections with workgroups docked at the bottom, and a floating chat.
conversion_notes: Non-terminal surfaces form the top row in host order (dock_left, home_main by slot, dock_right, dock_top, then floating), terminal sections form the bottom row by slot; the column is 0.6 over 0.4.
Row proportions come from each surface's flex_weight, normalized; all weights here are 1.
editor_panel_2's active browser becomes a browser tab bound to its session and stays the active tab.
editor_panel_3 was hidden but held a tab, so it becomes a collapsed panel; editor_panel_4 was hidden and empty, so it is dropped.

Each workgroup pane becomes its own terminal tab terminal:<terminal_session_id>, bound to its existing session; a pane's own tab title becomes the tab's user label; section and workgroup titles are not carried.
The floating chat returns to the fixed column, shown, at the window's default width.
The v2 revision is the v1 layout_revision plus one, and the conversion emits one workspace.layout_changed with change migrated_from_v1 (Plans/Contracts_V0.md#CV-361).
